analysis.investment_thesis: Crompton is a solid consumer electricals franchise but at ₹17,088 Cr market cap and 34x P/E, it is a large-cap masquerading as a growth story — precisely the kind of crowded, over-owned name I avoid. Revenue growing at only 9.8% CAGR while the stock demands a premium typically reserved for 25%+ growers makes the risk-reward deeply unfavorable.
key_strengths: Near-zero debt (D/E 0.05) with consistently positive FCF across all 5 years
Dominant brand in fans and pumps with scale across multiple consumer durable categories
EBITDA recovering to ₹950 Cr in FY25, margins trending back up after Butterfly acquisition drag
key_risks: Revenue CAGR of only 9.8% over 7 years is far too slow to justify a 34x P/E multiple
Net profit peaked at ₹617 Cr in FY21 and still hasn't recovered — FY25 profit of ₹564 Cr is below that peak despite 7 years of revenue growth
No meaningful promoter holding (company was carved out of CG Power); skin-in-the-game is absent
red_flags: Market cap of ₹17,088 Cr is 8-17x outside my sweet spot of ₹100-2,000 Cr
P/E at 34.4x for a 9-10% growth business — value destruction waiting to happen
Profit growth CAGR of 8.2% over 7Y is slower than nominal GDP — this is not a multibagger
analysis.detailed_analysis: Crompton checks none of the SMILE boxes. It is large, institutional-owned (DII 65.7%), and priced as if it were a premium consumer brand when its operating margin sits at a thin 7.99%. The Butterfly acquisition in FY22 spiked debt to ₹1,686 Cr and caused ROE and profit compression that the company is still recovering from three years later — a cautionary tale on acquisition-led growth in commoditizing categories. The consumer electricals space (fans, pumps, lighting, appliances) faces structural margin pressure from commodity costs, aggressive Chinese competition, and private-label threat. Crompton's brand moat is real but narrow. At ₹261, investors are paying 35x earnings for a business growing revenues at ~10%, with no promoter backing and margins barely at 8%. The compounding math simply does not work for me — I need 10-50x returns, and Crompton at best delivers 2-3x over a decade.
